we propose an approach for color modeling of 3D objects from multiple views that (1) produces more realistic colors for non Lambertian surfaces and (seamlessly) integrates colors from multiple views, (2) is more efficient and (3) outperforms competing methods in a user study.
we introduce a method to efficiently estimate high-quality color models from a collection of 2D images of a 3D mesh, and that the method outperforms the state of the art.

we introduce a novel approach to estimate a color model of a 3D mesh given RGB images of the object, which produces qualitatively superior results than those produced by other methods, and we introduce practical strategies to speed up the optimization.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the problem of high-quality 3-D color modeling from multiple RGB images is well-posed, and can be solved efficiently using a non-linear least-squares optimization approach.
a simple, non-iterative, least squares optimization approach, when combined with appropriate regularization terms, produces high-quality colored 3D models.
